title: Normalized ramified proper/open support comparison
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite-field datum D of characteristic p≠l, finite extensions E⊂L of Q_l, ramification e≥1, and a separated finite-type morphism f:X→Y of separated finite-type D.k-schemes with compactification c. Let a be Context data for the actual strict coefficient-system operations, integral compact support and exceptional adjunctions [def-coef-finite-scalar-mate-data], and P the normalized preparation of [lem-coef-ramified-scalar-preparation]. Define supportSource and supportTarget by the explicit compositions in that preparation: cofinal restriction, inverse exceptional reduction comparison, inverse scalar-reduction comparison followed by upper support realization on one side; cofinal restriction, inverse exceptional and support reduction comparisons, then scalar-model inverse on the other. For every integral constructible M on Y, retainedLimit maps a.alpha at a.r.G(a.RY M), followed by P.supportSource at M, equals P.supportTarget at M followed by the prescribed integralAlphaComponent at a.GR M. This is only the proper/open support square; it asserts no existence of a Context, preparation, exceptional limit realization, or exceptional coefficient transpose.

proof.text: Expand the defined support identifications. Naturality of cofinal restriction moves the actual system comparison through the retained-limit map; naturality of the proper/open scalar arrow moves the inverse exceptional-reduction comparison to the input. This reduces the calculation to the coherent reduction of the integral object a.GR M.

Under steps 3 and 5, the total limit of $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ is the limit of its specified proper coefficient projection followed by the open coefficient identification, evaluated on the actual reduction system of $P=G_RM$. This is precisely the ordered strict-tower composite defining $c_{S/R,P}$ in the integral compact-support coefficient-comparison theorem. The system-transpose theorem specifies $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ by that same simultaneous construction and finite-free normalization; its quotient compatibility is an identity before limit. Thus the maps agree before applying total limit, after the stated system isomorphisms. The integral comparison theorem uses $\chi$ to pass to strict scalar extension, giving exactly $\alpha_{G_RM}$. Naturality follows by composing the functorial counits, scalar reassociations, $\chi$, arithmetic restriction and the specified system functors. Projection identities and their scalar adjoints follow from the counit description and $p_n\rho_e=p_{en}$. No equality of system maps has been inferred solely from equality of their evaluations.

theorem supportComparison (e : ℕ)
    (he : PurCompactSupport.Ramification l E L i e) (hp : 1 ≤ e)
    (a : Context l E L i D hl f c)
    (P : RamifiedScalarPreparation.Preparation a e he hp)
    (M : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E Y) :
    (retainedLimit l L Y e).map ((a.alpha.app (a.r.G.obj (a.RY.obj M))).hom) ≫
        P.supportSource.hom.app M =
      P.supportTarget.hom.app M ≫ a.integralAlphaComponent (a.GR.obj M)
